root_cause.text: In `drivers/md/raid5.c`, `need_this_block()` failed to apply the llbitmap `blocks_synced()` check used during dirtying, so on degraded arrays a new write to an unwritten bitmap region could incorrectly avoid forcing RCW and leave `handle_stripe()` stuck in a no-progress loop (`handle_stripe_fill()` with `need_this_block()` always returning 0).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mddev = sh->raid_conf->mddev` and sets `force_rcw = true` when `mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(mddev, sh->sector)` is false, with the commit message explicitly stating that this check was already done in `handle_stripe_dirtying()` but missing in `need_this_block()`, causing the stripe to deadloop and I/O hang.

intent_record.intent_summary: Expand force_rcw selection to also respect bitmap sync state, ensuring unsynced blocks trigger the correct parity handling path.
intent_record.what: The code changed the initialization of `force_rcw` from a single boolean expression based only on `sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW` to a separate `bool force_rcw = false;` followed by a conditional that sets it true when either RMW is disabled or when `mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced()` exists and reports the block is not synced. It also introduces a local `struct mddev *mddev = sh->raid_conf->mddev;` variable.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will now force read-modify-write avoidance behavior more broadly: not only when RMW is explicitly disabled, but also when the bitmap layer indicates the stripe's blocks are not yet synchronized. This makes the code choose the more conservative RCW path in cases where data consistency requires it.

grouping_result.intent: Expand force_rcw selection to also respect bitmap sync state, ensuring unsynced blocks trigger the correct parity handling path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds bitmap sync-state awareness to force_rcw selection, which is the missing logic in need_this_block() that caused unwritten bitmap regions on degraded arrays to skip RCW and stall handle_stripe().

This is part of the pre-fix decision path for whether to force RCW, but it lacks any llbitmap blocks_synced() check. The bug is that the selection logic did not account for unsynced bitmap blocks, allowing the wrong parity handling path.

This condition contributes to the pre-fix force_rcw decision, but it also omits bitmap synchronization state. Without checking whether the block is synced, the code can incorrectly avoid RCW on a new write to an unwritten bitmap region.

Because of that omission, writes into unwritten bitmap regions on degraded arrays could fail to force RCW and leave `handle_stripe()` stuck.

This is part of the pre-fix RCW decision path in `need_this_block()`, but it does not incorporate llbitmap sync-state awareness. The missing `blocks_synced()` gating here allows the incorrect no-RCW path on unsynced blocks.

The bug described was that `need_this_block()` failed to apply the llbitmap `blocks_synced()` check used during dirtying, causing a degraded-array write to an unwritten bitmap region to avoid forcing RCW and potentially loop. In the provided snippet, there is no `blocks_synced()` check at all, and the added logic only introduces `bool force_rcw = (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW);` plus extra degraded-raid6 handling: `if (s->failed >= 2 && (fdev[i]->towrite || s->failed_num[i] == sh->pd_idx || s->failed_num[i] == sh->qd_idx) && !test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &fdev[i]->flags)) force_rcw = true;`. That is about forcing reconstruct-write in max-degraded raid6, not about llbitmap synchronization state. The later check `if (!force_rcw && sh->sector < sh->raid_conf->mddev->recovery_cp) return 0;` is also unrelated to bitmap unwritten-region handling. So the vulnerable statement is absent, and this commit does not already show the llbitmap fix.
